nodes.mul_nie.text.t: "So do people. But a man won't carry sixty kilos of pots for me." The tinker lets go of your sleeve and grabs the next one. The next one is a coat stand.

nodes.mul_prosba.options.[nie].text.t: It's war, old man. Mules die.

nodes.mul_prosba.text.t: The old tinker catches you by the sleeve. "Have you seen a mule? Grey, with a rope round his neck. Answers to Emperor. I named him before it was dangerous, because he eats for ten and never does what he should. For three days I've been going round the camp shouting that Emperor has run off, and twice already they've hauled me in for questioning. He went toward the burnt village, there's still cabbage there. Will you bring him back? Without the mule I'm just an old man with pots."

nodes.mul_tak.text.t: "God give you health, and I'll give you thirty groats, because God doesn't pay me. Just be firm with him. He doesn't react to 'whoa'. To 'Your Highness' sometimes he does."

nodes.mul_zwrot.text.t: Ziemowit runs out from under the canvas, and the mule looks at him as if it were the tinker who'd got lost. "You're alive, you swine! Your Highness, you swine!" A soldier by the cart lifts his head, thinks it over and goes back to his nap. The tinker counts out your coins and throws in something from the sack. "Take some herbs too. My wife gathered them. Long ago, so they're strong."

nodes.plotki.text.t: "The captain's in a foul mood because the staff write orders but don't write what to shoot with. The healer's in a foul mood because her lads keep getting carried in. And I'm in a foul mood because someone nicked my spare ladle. The crows in the field behind camp have gorged so much they don't fly any more, they walk. That's all I know. The rest you'll hear from the lot at that table, but they lie."

nodes.podrozny.options.[wojna].text.t: Why push on toward the front?

nodes.podrozny.text.t: Under the canvas sits an old tinker with a sack of pots that nobody cooks in any more. "Ziemowit. I go where they still have holes in their pots and not yet in their heads. Less and less of that about."

nodes.podrozny_droga.text.t: "Don't go east, unless you fancy hanging. There's a hill there where you can see from afar who's late with his taxes. And in the ravine behind the forest sit deserters. Decent folk, they gave me a pot to mend. Well, took mine, but they said good day first."

nodes.podrozny_wojna.text.t: "Because the army is the best customer. They put holes in his pots, they put holes in his helmets, and he still has pay. Well, had. Now I take buttons. I've got half a sack of buttons already and not one decent coat to go with them."

nodes.powitanie.options.[handel].text.t: Show me what you've got for sale.

nodes.powitanie.options.[mul_prosba].tex.t: The old man's looking for his mule.

nodes.powitanie.options.[stol].text.t: I'll sit down with the soldiers.

nodes.powitanie.options.[stol_zimno].tex.t: I'll sit down with the soldiers.

nodes.powitanie.options.[zegota_zwrot].t.t: For the corporal: I've got the purse.

nodes.powitanie.options.[zupa].text.t: A bowl of soup and a hunk of bread (8 gr).

nodes.powitanie.text.t: The sutler's tent is a sheet of canvas on four poles, two tables made of somebody's doors, and a cauldron. Soldiers dice at one table; at the other sit the ones who are only passing through. Behind the cauldron stands a broad woman with a ladle like a mace. "Bronka. Soup's hot, beer's wet, and the only ones who eat on credit here are the dead. Sit down or get out of the way."

nodes.stol.options.[jarnowianie].text.t: What sort of people are these Jarnowians?

nodes.stol.text.t: The soldiers shift over half a buttock, and Corporal Żegota, a man with a face like an old sack, slides a mug toward you. Somebody else's, but full. "Sit. Just no talking about the battle, we're eating."

nodes.stol_front.text.t: "The front is wherever you happen to step in shit. Yesterday it was past the crossing. Today it's supposedly in the burnt village, because the imperial scouts are sitting in the thickets there, counting who goes for water. If you go, it won't be for water."

nodes.stol_jarnowianie.text.t: "The same as us, just from the other side of the river. Their camp is two days from here, they don't get paid either, and they've got a corporal who talks over his soup. Swap us over and nobody would notice. Except for the corporal. Their corporal has both eyes."

nodes.stol_kosci.text.t: The soldier next to him tips three buttons and a tooth onto the table. "For the buttons. And for the tooth, but the tooth is Domasław's and Domasław wants it back." Domasław nods and presses a rag to his gum, because the hole where the tooth was is still bleeding.

nodes.stol_zimno.text.t: Nobody shifts over. Żegota looks into his mug as if it were more interesting in there. "The gambler didn't have a purse, did he? Pity, then. No room either. There's plenty of room under the canvas, that's where the ones who are only passing through sit."

nodes.wiesc_falsz.text.t: "Word is forty islanders went to the fort looking for wagons that weren't there. They came for powder and left under crossbow fire. The army's so pleased that two of them even paid for their soup. I've never seen that before."

nodes.wiesc_powrot.text.t: "They're back. Thirty-two more mouths for the cauldron, and the same purse. The sergeant came and asked how much he owed them for soup. Never seen that before either. I gave it to him free, but don't tell anyone."

nodes.wiesc_prawda.text.t: "They burned the wagon train at the crossing. Staszek the carter ate here, he owed me for two soups. I don't know who sold them out, but when I find out, he'll get soup made of whatever's lying behind the cauldron. There's no powder, so today we're all foot soldiers, even the gunners."

nodes.wiesc_proch.text.t: "The islanders shoot wet powder. So they say. Ours waded through the ford as if nobody was there and came back with three chests of somebody else's hardtack. Hard as a boot heel, but they're ours. Well, not ours. You know what I mean."

nodes.wiesc_ucieczka.text.t: "Gone, so they say. Thirty men. The captain's raging that he has nobody to hang, and at the table, funnily enough, they're cheerful. Somebody must have helped them, they'd never have found the fence on their own."

nodes.wiesc_wydani.text.t: "What's to say? They hung yesterday, they hang today. The corporal says two of them used to eat at that table, back when there was something to eat." Bronka stirs longer than the soup needs. "You've got your soup today. But I don't know what you came here for."

nodes.zegota_klamstwo.text.t: "Drank it." Żegota repeats it without anger, the way you'd repeat how many days are left till harvest. Nearby someone stops rolling the dice. In your pouch sixty groats weigh exactly what they should, and the sutler's tent feels somehow more cramped.

nodes.zegota_nie.text.t: "Clever clogs. You shouldn't have gone to war either, and yet here we sit." Żegota goes back to his mug. "If you change your mind, you know where the table is."

nodes.zegota_noga.text.t: Żegota taps his spoon against his knee. It sounds like wood. "This one. I've got the other one too, but this one won't walk on its own."

nodes.zegota_oddane.text.t: Żegota counts twice, then lets Domasław count, who counts on his fingers and stops at thirty, because that's as far as he goes. He pushes a handful of coins toward you. "Twenty-five. The squad chipped in. Don't cry, we're not family, it's just that nobody's given us anything back in a long time."

nodes.zegota_polowa.text.t: Żegota looks at you for a long time, then at half the purse. "Thirty. The gambler took everything and you took half. That makes you twice as honest." He counts it out. Nobody thanks you, but nobody takes the mug away either.

nodes.zegota_prosba.text.t: "You. You look like you can count to three. There was a gambler here, Mszczuj, thin as wire. He sat down with us on payday and after two jugs he had the whole squad's pay. Sixty groats. Loaded dice, I'd swear to it if I could see straight at the time. He went off to the field, trade's better there. Get the purse back and you'll get a cut. The captain won't let us leave, and I won't go myself, on account of my leg."

nodes.zegota_tak.text.t: "The cart stands at the edge of the field, you can't miss it, it's the only cart with all its wheels. Mszczuj has two sack-carriers with him. Don't play him. I'm telling you because nobody told me."

nodes.zegota_zwrot.options.[klamstwo].te.t: He didn't. He drank the lot.

nodes.zegota_zwrot.options.[polowa].text.t: He did. Half is mine, for the trouble.

nodes.zegota_zwrot.text.t: The corporal puts down his spoon. The table goes quiet, only Domasław keeps sucking his gum. "Well? Did he have the purse on him?"

nodes.znowu.options.[handel].text.t: Show me what you've got for sale.

nodes.znowu.options.[mul_prosba].text.t: The old man's looking for his mule.

nodes.znowu.options.[stol].text.t: I'll sit down with the soldiers.

nodes.znowu.options.[stol_zimno].text.t: I'll sit down with the soldiers.

nodes.znowu.options.[zegota_zwrot].text.t: For the corporal: I've got the purse.

nodes.znowu.options.[zupa].text.t: A bowl of soup and a hunk of bread (8 gr).

nodes.znowu.text.t: Bronka doesn't look up from the cauldron. "You again? Same soup, only thicker. Don't ask why."

nodes.zupa.text.t: You get a bowl with something in it that might have been porridge, and a hunk of bread hard as a boot heel. It's hot. At the front that's enough to call it dinner. "There was meat on Monday," says Bronka. "Which Monday, I won't say."
